According to Liverpool's seasoned defender Andy Robertson, the primary determinant for the club's success under new manager Arne Slot will be a significant and sustained improvement in their defensive fortitude. Robertson posits that for Liverpool to mount a credible challenge for the league title during Slot’s inaugural season, shoring up the backline is not just beneficial but absolutely essential. The early indications under the new leadership have been decidedly positive, with the team successfully preventing any goals from being scored against them in their first two competitive outings. This initial defensive perfection, which saw them nullify the offensive efforts of both Ipswich and Brentford, has provided Slot with an ideal foundation upon which to build his tenure. However, this promising start is set against the backdrop of a much more challenging fixture on the horizon. A trip to face their rivals Manchester United is expected to serve as a true litmus test for this renewed defensive resolve, presenting a far more potent and severe examination of their capabilities than they have faced thus far. This early-season performance stands in stark contrast to their record from the previous campaign, where their defensive frailties were a noticeable weakness. Finishing in third place, the team conceded a total of 41 goals across the 38-game season, a figure that was considerably higher than their main competitors. This number was seven more than the champions, Manchester City, and a significant twelve more than the runners-up, Arsenal, highlighting a clear area for improvement if they hope to contend at the highest level once again.

Handle the offensive threats of more formidable opponents is the true measure of their progress, and the upcoming match against Manchester United represents the first such major hurdle. The clean sheets against Ipswich and Brentford, while valuable for building confidence and momentum, were achieved against opposition that does not possess the same level of attacking firepower as the league's elite. The true test, as implied by the context of the upcoming fixture, will be whether Liverpool’s defensive system can withstand the pressure applied by a top-tier rival in a high-stakes environment. Looking back, the statistical evidence from last season paints a clear picture of why a defensive overhaul was necessary. The 41 goals they allowed were a key factor in their inability to keep pace with Manchester City and Arsenal down the stretch. That defensive gap—conceding a dozen more goals than Arsenal—translates directly into dropped points and lost opportunities over the long and grueling marathon of a Premier League season. A defense that porous ultimately undermines the efforts of the attack and makes a consistent title bid nearly impossible to sustain, as it places an immense burden on the forwards to outscore the opposition in almost every single match, which is an unrealistic expectation for any team, no matter how potent its attack may be.

Reflecting on the team's performance, Robertson himself articulated this new emphasis on defensive stability and expressed his satisfaction with the immediate results. He pointed to the two clean sheets as the best possible start they could have envisioned, establishing a standard they are eager to maintain. Looking forward, the defender articulated a clear objective: to continue this defensive solidity by effectively neutralizing the scoring opportunities for Manchester United. This goal extends beyond a single match, with Robertson stating the team’s ambition to similarly limit the chances of all their opponents following the upcoming international break. He drew a direct line from this new focus to the shortcomings of the previous season, astutely analyzing that even when Liverpool was still mathematically in the title race, their underlying defensive metrics were a cause for concern. Robertson noted that the team was likely allowing more high-quality chances to their opponents than either Arsenal or Manchester City. He concluded with a poignant reflection on the inevitable consequences of such defensive laxity, explaining that when a team consistently gives up numerous chances, it is only a matter of time before a game arrives where they are decisively punished for it, a fate that ultimately befell Liverpool and derailed their championship aspirations.

P.S. The analysis provided is a detailed paraphrase and expansion based solely on the excerpt given from the Guardian news article.
